title: feat(pm/fleet-write): sub_issue_add and sub_issue_remove — an epic PM links a parent's children as objectstack-fleet[bot], read back from the parent's sub_issues list
body:
Fixes #27301
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:舰队写中继的闭合 op 表新增 `sub_issue_add` / `sub_issue_remove` 两个 op,云席位以 `objectstack-fleet[bot]` 身份把子卡挂到父卡下,或从父卡摘下。
- 为什么改:中继此前没有挂子卡的通道,epic PM 只能用个人账号直连挂子卡,破坏「写侧恒为 fleet bot」;子树挂不上,epic 队列读数与半态巡查就看不到子卡。
- 风险与回滚:只动 `scripts/pm/fleet-write/**` 四个文件与一份 PM 参考文档,不发布任何包、不改 workflow;回滚即 revert 本 PR。写前核对两张卡,写后回读父卡的子卡列表才算落地,任何不符都是零写入或明确失败。
- 先看:`scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs`(`subIssuePreflight` 与 `confirmSubIssue`,风险在写前围栏与回读窗口)、`scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs`(两行 op 与 `SUB_ISSUE_FENCES`)、`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/rest-channel.md`(新增一行、删去一行)。
- 两分钟验证:`node scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs --self-test`,预期末行 `208 cases pass across 20 batteries`。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地(Tier S;首次真实挂卡由席位在合入后执行)。

## What changes

The fleet-write relay's closed op table gains the pair the card asks for, each with fences and a measured read-back. A cloud seat can now write an issue-hierarchy link as `objectstack-fleet[bot]` instead of under a person's login.

- `scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs`
  - Adds a header section, "The two rows that write an issue's hierarchy".
  - Adds the field `sub_issue` (an integer; the child's issue NUMBER).
  - Adds the rows `sub_issue_add` (`POST .../issues/{parent}/sub_issues`) and `sub_issue_remove` (`DELETE .../issues/{parent}/sub_issue`, the platform's singular path). Both require `issue` and `sub_issue` and spend `issues` with no `alsoSpends`. Neither is `alone`. Each carries a new row property, `distinct: ['issue', 'sub_issue']`.
  - The descriptor carries `subIssue: { mode, parent, child }` and no body. The executor builds `{ sub_issue_id }` from the child's own answer and never sends `replace_parent`.
  - Adds the pure parts both other files read: `SUB_ISSUE_FENCES` (parent, child, free for add, listed for remove), `subIssueFenceFailures`, `subIssueFenceText`, `subIssueCardFailure`, `subIssueAlreadyHere`, `subIssueReadBack` and `subIssueLandedText`.
- `scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs`
  - Adds a header section, "The hierarchy link".
  - `subIssuePreflight` reads the parent's and the child's own `GET .../issues/{n}`. Only when both pass does it read the child's `GET .../issues/{child}/parent` (add) or the parent's whole `GET .../issues/{parent}/sub_issues` list (remove: every page at 100, capped at 10 pages, and a truncated list is a SUBSET, never read as absent). It then judges every fence, so a failing fence means the write is NOT SENT and zero writes happen.
  - An add whose child already answers to THIS parent is a measured no-op: nothing is sent, and it lands only when the list reads the child back.
  - `confirmSubIssue` lands a write only when the parent's list lists the child's id (add) or no longer does (remove). It re-reads every 3 s for up to 30 s. A non-2xx answer is FAILED with nothing read back. A list that never settles is FAILED UNCONFIRMED, ⛔ never re-sent.
- `scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs`
  - Adds a header bullet and the `distinct` rule: an action naming one issue as both parent and child is refused by name, judged only on values the field kinds admitted.
  - Adds the two rows to the three minimal-shape ledgers and the refused-family sample.
- `scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs`
  - Adds a header bullet: neither row carries a body, so the seat reads nothing back. A `success` run is the executor's confirmation, as for `pr_update_branch`. Neither row is content-creating, so an epic's links are paced at rule ①'s gap.
- `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/rest-channel.md` (80 → 80, ceiling 80)
  - Adds a write-side row after the `pr_update_branch` row (112 B, no ✓ because the op has not been called live):

    ```text
    - 挂子卡走中继 op `sub_issue_add`/`sub_issue_remove`(`issue` 父号,`sub_issue` 子号),回读父列表。
    ```

  - The row is paid for by deleting this line from the 第三桶 section:

    ```text
    - 本表只指路,⛔ 不在两处各存一份;先问 git,再问 REST。
    ```

    That content already has a home: the git-before-REST read order is `references/reading-discipline.md` L35 (`读序 git、payload、REST、MCP`), and the pointer to `platform-readings.md` stays on the line above.

No `.github/workflows/**` change is needed. GitHub's server-to-server permission ledger lists `add-sub-issue` and `remove-sub-issue` under `issues: write` with no additional permission, and `fleet-write.yml` already mints `permission-issues: write` literally on every stroke.

## Acceptance notes

- Mechanism readings, all measured:
  - Paths and bodies come from GitHub's REST OpenAPI description (`issues/add-sub-issue`, `issues/remove-sub-issue`, `issues/list-sub-issues`, `issues/get-parent`), read 2026-10-29. The add returns 201 and the remove 200, each answering an issue object.
  - The permission rows come from `github/docs` `server-to-server-permissions.json`: `issues` write, server-to-server, `additional-permissions: false`.
  - Read-only REST GETs against this repository made zero writes:
    - `#27293/sub_issues` listed 10 children by REST id.
    - `#26709` carries `parent_issue_url`, but `#27301`, which has no parent, omits the field entirely.
    - `#27301/parent` answered 404 `No parent issue found`.
    - `#26709/parent` answered 200 with #27293.
  - Because a missing field is not evidence, the add's `free` fence reads the `/parent` endpoint and does not infer absence from a missing field.
- Design choices the seat may want to re-rule:
  - The payload carries the child's NUMBER and never `sub_issue_id`, which the card allowed as an alternative. Resolving the id from the number keeps the payload in the vocabulary every other row uses.
  - An add whose child is already under this same parent is a measured no-op that lands with zero writes. A remove of a child the parent does not list is refused, as the order spells it.
  - The read-back window is 30 s (`SUB_ISSUE_WINDOW_MS`). The first failure stops a stroke, so at most one window is paid.
- ⛔ The new op was never exercised against the live repository. The first live stroke is the seat's, after landing.
- Not touched: `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` H45 and `seat-lifecycle.md` 〈Epic 子树车道〉. They already read `sub_issues_summary`; this PR only gives them a writer.

That includes `check:pm-fleet-write-validate`, `-execute` and `-dispatch` (the last also runs `rerun-failed.mjs --self-test`), `check:pm-skill-ratchet`, `check:pm-skill-id-lint`, `check:pm-governed-merges`, `check:self-test-wired`, `check:nul-bytes` and `check:pm-dispatch-gates` (fast tier: 1935 cases, 7 slow sections deferred).
